checks.evidence: verify defaults: PASS finite, peak_db -1.00, silent_edges -200/-200, dc -93 dB, rebuild bit-identical, macro brightness and length claims; no FAIL.

time_shape.evidence: Silence first: leading silence 2.087 s (seed 1; 2.9-3.2 s for seeds 2-4), length 14 s (in 6-14). Decay -60 dB at 7.11 s is long on paper, but in the seed-1 picture and loudness curve the body is five bursts from 2.08 to ~4.6 s (loudness under -48 LUFS by ~5 s, decay -20 dB only 1.72 s), then 4.1 s of trailing silence from 9.86 s with only faint ticks after 5 s. Reads as a short cluster of hits with a thin tail, not a long rolling decay; the tail is longer in seeds 2-3 (energy to ~10 s).

spectrum.evidence: Centroid 54/38/29 Hz start/middle/end (whole 54 Hz, under 150); 98% of energy below 200 Hz; 63 Hz band is dominant at start/middle (-30 dB vs -36 at 125 Hz, -41 at 250 Hz), falling to near nothing above 2 kHz. Centroid falls over time. Brightness macro at 1 gives start centroid 143 Hz, still under 150.

parts.evidence: Brief names silence then a rumble. Silence 0-2.087 s is clean; a crack/onset at 2.123 s (centroid 99 Hz, 0.75 ms attack, strength 0.9) is distinct from the later rumble bursts at 2.741, 3.733, 4.427 s (centroids 45-62 Hz); spectrogram shows broadband vertical crack lines up to ~2-4 kHz over a 30-60 Hz rumble.

control_variation.evidence: Two macros (brightness, length), both claims PASS: centroid 39/43/54/83/143 Hz; decay 4.62/6.64/7.77/9.43/11.15 s. Seeds differ measurably: leading silence 2.09/2.94/3.12/3.21 s, onsets 5/5/1/7, loudness -29.8/-27.0/-25.4/-24.9 LUFS, decay60 7.1/7.6/7.1/4.8 s; all have centroid ~47-54 Hz at start, >97% under 200 Hz, silence first.

notes: Seed-1 loudness is -29.8 LUFS, about 5 LU quieter than seed 4 (-24.9), so seeds vary a lot in level.
Seed 4 reports attack 3.2 s and a silence window (start 3.21 s, end 2.76 s) that does not line up, so its silence descriptors are unreliable.
Descriptor modes at 816 Hz and 1.05 kHz (60 ms) come from the crack transients; the picture shows isolated vertical lines up to 2-4 kHz, so the crack is a series of discrete spikes.
